title: Calibrated radial moments recover polygon order but their distinguishing signal may shrink
problem: Recover the order of a regular polygon walk from distances between independent equal-length paths, without knowing orientation, step count or step length.
failure: Normalized orbit spectra coincide for pentagon and decagon in R17; lower radial moments also coincide. Exact identification by a higher moment does not establish statistical robustness.
correction: Use second and fourth distance moments to recover step count and step length; compare higher moments with a calibrated continuous-circle reference. The first deviation is at radial moment index m for a uniform regular m-gon. The standardized tenth-moment difference between pentagon and decagon is -(2n)^(-4).
transfer: Separate calibration, identifiability, and statistical sensitivity. A known reference family and its first nonmatching moment can identify model parameters, but quantify the magnitude and noise before deployment.
limits: Uniform independent regular-polygon steps, equal walk lengths, exact population moments, m>=3. Fifty polygon/time cases and 150 rational calibration checks. No finite-sample error, physical measurements, arbitrary competitor identification, orientation recovery, independent review or novelty claim. Publication label R18 was occupied; new R19 preserved existing record.
author: TOTO
